transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Well… it’s kind of embarrassing, but I’m here because I’ve gotten so worked up about wasps that I plan my whole summer around avoiding them. I used to help with the garden jobs at church, you know, the flower beds and that sort of thing—my mother always liked keeping things tidy outside too—but now I’ve pretty much given that up.

And at home, if I hear buzzing near the back porch, I make my husband unload things instead of me going out there. It sounds silly when I say it, but it’s gotten to where it’s running too much of what I do.
How long have you felt this way about wasps, and does the fear happen every time you think about or encounter them?

It really started after our remodel, when they uncovered a wasp nest—oh, that was such a mess, the whole back side of the house was torn up and I remember thinking we should’ve waited until fall. Anyway… that was about two years and five months ago now. Since then it’s just been hard for me to be around them, or even think they might be nearby.
When you’re around wasps or even just think about them, do you notice your heart racing, sweating, shaking, or feeling like you need to get out of the situation right away?

Yes—right away, honestly. The second I hear that sharp buzzing by the porch, or if I see one hovering near the flowers, my heart just jumps. My hands start shaking, and I feel like I have to get inside immediately.

It’s funny, I used to love being out by the flowers—well, not funny exactly, but you know what I mean. Now even one little sound and I’m already halfway to the door.
Do you find yourself avoiding places or activities where you think wasps might be, even if you don’t actually see or hear them at the time?

Yes, I do. I’ve gotten so I sort of plan the whole summer around where wasps might be, even if I haven’t seen one yet. Like with the garden jobs at church—I used to do the flower beds, and there was this one lady who always planted marigolds, and I’d fuss over them too—but now I just don’t sign up for it because I’m sure there’ll be wasps around.

And at home, near the back porch, if I even think I hear buzzing, I’ll ask my husband to unload things or go out there instead of me. It feels over the top, but I just can’t seem to make myself go.
